dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: atattvam indrajālābham idaṃ sarvam avasthitam | kiṃ tattvam indrajālasya iti dārḍhyāc chamaṃ vrajet ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 133: GRETIL and Wallis read indrajālasya iti; Pradīpaka applies sandhi (indrajālasyeti).
dharana.rendering: 'This whole world stands without essential reality, like a magic show; what reality does a magic show have?' Through firmness in this, one attains peace.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh comments on verses 133 and 134 together: both concern the unreality of the world; 133 says the world is like a magic show and therefore has no reality, and contemplating so, one acquires peace. Wallis: 'all this is a magic show'. Compare verse 102 (D-079), where seeing the world as a magic show brings happiness.
dharana.technique_name: All This Is Like a Magic Show
dharana.instruction: Hold firmly the view that all this is like a magic show, and let peace settle in.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 108' = verse 133 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 133 = 'All this is a magic show (Y108 ~ B2)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 133 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 133: All this is a magic show (Y108 ~ B2)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 133 'Dharana 110', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 108. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 133 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the peace of not taking it as solid
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the world as a stage show: vivid, convincing, and without solid reality behind it.
geometry.svg_hint: a stage with simple figures drawn in light lines and nothing behind the backdrop
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: It's a show
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a world taken as solid is seen as a magic show, and the grip on it relaxes into peace. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The world seen as a magic show, without essential reality
attention.secondary: Peace through firmly holding that view

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: 'This whole world stands without essential reality, like a magic show; what reality does a magic show have?' Through firmness in this, one attains peace.
adiyogi.method_summary: Look at what appears (events, objects, your own roles) and ask: how real is a magic show? Hold the view firmly that all this, however vivid, is like a magic show, and let the peace of that settle in.

honesty.disclosure: Door 108 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 108 (verse 133) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 108 is dharana 108, verse 133. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. This view is for loosening inner grip, not for dismissing responsibility or anyone's suffering. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
